- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — adjust downward bias to match recent low trend.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak in high-sentiment windows.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment is strong.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment rises sharply 3–5 days before forecast, adjust forecast to reflect early momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term volatility — if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, reduce forecast volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently >0.6, reduce forecast slope downward to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment drops after forecast peak, reduce forecast by 2–4% per day of declining sentiment.
